key: A see-saw with the pivot moved close
name: ch01_seesaw_pivot_leverage
alt: Two see-saws in a park: one with the pivot in the middle moving both ends equally, one with the pivot near the trader so a small push flings his seat high.
scene: A wide two-panel view of a small Indian neighbourhood park on a bright morning, a neem tree and a row of iron benches in the background, the two panels split by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an ordinary metal see-saw with its pivot exactly in the middle. A calm man in his thirties wearing a cream kurta and holding a folded share certificate sits on the near end; on the far end a small child gives a gentle push, and both ends move by the same modest amount, shown by two equal curved arrows. RIGHT panel: the same man sits on a see-saw whose pivot has been slid right up close to his seat, so his end is very short and the far end is very long. A little boy at the far end taps it lightly with one finger, a tiny arrow on his side, and the man's seat swings violently through a huge arc, a long curved arrow showing him flung high into the air, eyes wide, clutching the handle, a few coins flying out of his shirt pocket. A small inset bubble near the far end shows a price tag nudging up by a hair. The lighting is cheerful and clear so the size difference between the tiny push and the big swing is obvious. Labels: "FULL PAYMENT" above the left see-saw's pivot, "MARGIN" above the right see-saw's pivot, and "PRICE" beside the boy's finger on the right.

key: sends every driver down the same
name: ch01_nav_app_side_road_jam
alt: Many cars follow a phone app's suggestion into one narrow side road, which jams, while a few experienced drivers take other routes toward the same busy market.
scene: A high bird's-eye view of a busy Indian city junction in late-afternoon light, drawn like a small map come to life. In the foreground right, a large hand holds a generic smartphone showing a simple map with a bright route line pointing everyone into one narrow side road, with a little lightning-bolt icon reading "fastest". In the middle of the picture that same narrow lane, lined with small shops and a parked handcart, is jammed bumper to bumper with auto-rickshaws, hatchbacks and scooters, drivers leaning out of windows, one honking, one wiping his forehead. Above the lane the phone's route line has started to turn from green to red. On the left, two older drivers who know the city, a turbaned taxi driver and a woman on a scooter with a helmet, calmly take a wider main road around, one checking his watch as if he set off early. In the far background, at the end of every road, sits a crowded vegetable market with people carrying bags, the real destination everyone needs, with dotted arrows from all routes converging on it to show the traffic exists because people truly need to get there. Mood: busy but good-humoured. Labels: "EVERYONE SAME ROUTE" above the jammed lane, "SELF-CORRECTION" beside the drivers on the wide road, and "REAL DEMAND" over the market.

key: One stock is one voice in a noisy room
name: ch02_noisy_room_shared_hum
alt: A crowded hall where eleven people each shout about their own news, while a listener with a cupped ear hears only the low shared hum underneath.
scene: A wide interior view of a crowded old community hall with ceiling fans and tall shuttered windows, warm afternoon light slanting in. Eleven people of different ages stand in a loose half-circle, each shouting their own news with a small speech bubble containing a single tiny icon: a factory worker in a blue boiler suit with a raised fist and a strike placard icon, a businesswoman in a saree waving a signed contract icon, a lawyer in a black coat with a gavel icon, a farmer with a rain-cloud icon, a shopkeeper with a padlock icon and so on. The bubbles overlap and clash, drawn in many different colours. In the right foreground an elderly man with round spectacles and a notebook sits on a wooden chair, eyes closed, one hand cupped behind his ear. A single smooth wavy band, drawn as a soft grey ribbon, rises from beneath all eleven speakers and flows into his ear, while the coloured bubbles fade out before reaching him, showing the private shouting cancelling and only the shared tone remaining. On his notebook page is a simple steady line. Mood: noisy and busy on the left, calm and attentive on the right. Labels: "OWN NEWS" above the cluster of clashing bubbles, "SHARED HUM" along the grey ribbon, and "THE AVERAGE" on the listener's notebook.

key: someone whispers that the painting
name: ch02_auction_whisper_crack
alt: At an auction a whisper about a crack in the painting spreads and every bidder lowers their paddle at the same moment, before anyone reads the restorer's report.
scene: A mid-shot inside an elegant but slightly worn auction room in an old colonial building in Kolkata, wooden chairs in rows, chandeliers, a large oil painting of a river landscape on an easel at the front. At the front right, the auctioneer, a grey-haired man in a dark bandhgala jacket, stands at a lectern with his gavel raised, looking surprised. In the second row a young woman in a green salwar leans to whisper into her neighbour's ear, her hand shielding her mouth, and a thin wavy whisper line travels sideways along the rows, touching every bidder's ear in turn. All the bidders, men and women in formal clothes, are caught lowering their numbered paddles at the same instant, a small downward arrow beside each paddle. A large board on the wall behind shows the current bid dropping, the old figure crossed out. On a side table at the far left, ignored by everyone, sits a sealed brown envelope with a ribbon, the restorer's report, still unopened, a faint cobweb on it. A tiny magnifying-glass inset near the painting shows a hairline crack in the canvas. Lighting is warm and theatrical. Labels: "NEWS" beside the whisper line, "PRICE ALREADY MOVED" above the bid board, and "REPORT" on the unopened envelope.

key: a march with a big band behind it
name: ch02_march_band_vs_few_walkers
alt: Two processions climbing the same road: one swollen by a big brass band and a large crowd, the other just a few people walking quietly.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same gently rising village road lined with shops and marigold garlands, leading uphill to the right. LEFT panel: a big lively procession climbs the road, led by a full brass wedding band in red and gold uniforms with trumpets, a big drum and cymbals, followed by dozens of people of all ages, children on shoulders, women in bright sarees, men clapping, many more people joining from side lanes, a thick upward arrow running along the crowd. Musical notes fill the air and dust rises from the stamping feet. RIGHT panel: the same road, but only four people walk up it, two elderly men in white dhotis, a woman with a shopping bag and a boy kicking a stone, no music, the shops quiet, a dog asleep in the shade, and only a thin dotted arrow along their path. They are still climbing, but nobody important has joined; shopkeepers barely look up. Both panels share the same bright midday sun. Labels: "HEAVY VOLUME" at the top of the left panel, "THIN VOLUME" at the top of the right panel.

key: A runner who has been winning every
name: ch02_champion_runner_fading
alt: A champion runner wins, then misses her old best time and finally loses to a runner she used to beat, shown as three moments on a stadium track.
scene: A wide view of an outdoor athletics track at a district stadium, painted lanes, a concrete stand with a few spectators and a large manual scoreboard. The picture is a sequence of three moments from left to right along the track, like a strip. FIRST moment on the left: a confident young woman athlete in a red vest with bib number 7 breaks the finishing tape, arms raised, a small trophy icon above her and a stopwatch inset showing her best time. SECOND moment in the middle: the same athlete crosses the line again, now sweaty and frowning, with the stopwatch inset showing a slower time and a dotted line above her marking the old best she failed to reach. THIRD moment on the right: she is overtaken at the tape by a smaller runner in a blue vest with bib 12, whom the scoreboard earlier showed beaten by her, and she bends over hands-on-knees, clearly finished. A coach with a clipboard watches from the infield, writing notes. Between the first and second moments a brief stumble mark shows one slow lap that did not matter. Late afternoon golden light, long shadows. Labels: "FAILS AT OLD BEST" under the middle moment, "LOSES TO OLD RIVAL" under the right moment, and "TREND OVER" on the coach's clipboard.

key: The ball hitting the crossbar during
name: ch02_crossbar_vs_final_score
alt: A football striking the crossbar during a match is ignored by the scoreboard, which only records the final score at the whistle.
scene: A dynamic wide shot of a local football match on a dusty ground in Goa at dusk, coconut palms behind the low boundary wall, floodlights just switching on. On the left half, a young striker in a yellow jersey has just struck the ball and it slams against the crossbar of the goal, a big curved motion line and a star burst showing the impact, the goalkeeper in green diving helplessly underneath, spectators along the wall jumping up with mouths open. A thin dotted line from the crossbar leads away to a small thought bubble with a big cross through it, meaning it doesn't count. On the right half, a referee in black blows his whistle with arm raised to signal full time, and behind him a simple painted wooden scoreboard on poles shows the final score with large numbers, "2 - 1", lit by a single bulb. A man in a white shirt standing on a stool chalks the result into a ledger beside the scoreboard. The sky is deep orange fading to blue. Labels: "DURING THE DAY" near the crossbar, "THE CLOSE" above the scoreboard.

key: measures air pressure, which falls
name: ch02_barometer_before_rain
alt: A barometer on a verandah wall has already dropped while the sky is still sunny, and dark rain clouds are only just appearing on the horizon.
scene: A mid-shot of the wooden verandah of an old Kerala house with a tiled roof, looking out over a paddy field to distant hills. On the left, mounted on the whitewashed pillar, is a round brass barometer with a big needle that has clearly swung from the sunny side of the dial toward the stormy side, a curved arrow showing its downward swing. An elderly man in a white mundu and spectacles stands beside it tapping the glass with one finger, nodding knowingly, while his granddaughter in a school uniform holds an umbrella that is still closed. On the right, the scene outside is still bright: sunshine on the paddy, washing hanging on a line, a farmer working without worry. But on the far horizon a thin line of dark grey monsoon clouds is just beginning to rise, and a dotted arrow runs from the barometer needle across to those distant clouds to show the reading arrived first. A small clock inset near the barometer reads early morning, and a second small inset of rain hitting the field shows a later afternoon time. Lighting is warm and clear with a faint coolness creeping in from the right. Labels: "READING FALLS FIRST" under the barometer, "ECONOMY LATER" above the distant clouds.

key: Three ways to describe the same journey
name: ch03_three_travel_records
alt: A traveller's road trip recorded three ways on a table: a detailed diary, a short list of hotels, and a list of only the turns taken.
scene: A top-down view of a wooden table in a small hotel room, warm lamplight, a rucksack and a road map of Rajasthan lying open at the top edge with a winding red route drawn on it from one town to the next. Below the map, laid side by side from left to right, are three different records of the same trip. LEFT: a thick diary open to a full page per day, crammed with notes, small sketches of where the day started, a camel at the furthest point reached, a fort where the day ended, each day carefully boxed. MIDDLE: a single small notepad sheet with just a short column of hotel names and tiny bed icons, one per night, joined by a plain line. RIGHT: an index card showing only arrows for each turn made, left, right, left, with gaps where nothing happened and no dates at all. A young woman traveller in a denim jacket and a cotton scarf sits at the right edge of the table with a cup of chai, pen in hand, comparing them with a curious smile. A dotted line links each record back to the same red route on the map. Labels: "BAR CHART" under the diary, "LINE CHART" under the hotel list, and "POINT AND FIGURE" under the index card.

key: A school attendance register
name: ch03_attendance_register_columns
alt: A teacher's attendance register with one column per school day, no columns for weekends, and an empty column left in place for a holiday.
scene: A close, slightly angled view of a large cloth-bound school attendance register lying open on a teacher's wooden desk in an Indian government school classroom, a blackboard and a window with green shutters softly blurred behind. The open double page shows a grid: student names down the left margin in neat handwriting, and narrow date columns across the top, each filled with small ticks and the odd letter A. The columns run Monday to Friday and then jump straight to the next Monday, with no Saturday or Sunday columns at all; a small curved arrow above the page skips over the gap between Friday and Monday. One column in the middle is left completely blank, a thin pencil line through it and a tiny diya lamp sketched at its top for a festival holiday, and the columns on either side stay neatly aligned. A middle-aged woman teacher in a cotton saree and spectacles holds a fountain pen over the next empty column, about to mark the day. A stack of exercise books and a steel tiffin box sit at the desk's edge. Soft morning light falls across the page. Labels: "NO WEEKENDS" above the Friday-to-Monday arrow, "HOLIDAY LEFT EMPTY" under the blank column.

key: A hotel where every guest stays exactly
name: ch03_hotel_guests_occupancy
alt: A hotel cut open like a dollhouse where each guest's luggage grows and shrinks over their one-year stay, while a lobby board shows total occupancy.
scene: A cut-away front view of a five-storey hotel drawn like an open dollhouse, each room visible, set on a busy street at dusk with the hotel sign glowing. In each room a different guest is at a different stage of a year-long stay: on one floor a just-arrived young man in a hoodie stands beside a single small suitcase; next door a woman in a kurta has unpacked and her room is piled high with boxes and bags; above, an older couple is mid-stay with a moderate pile; another guest is busy packing, the pile shrinking, a taxi waiting outside; one room is empty, being cleaned by a housekeeper. Small arrows beside each pile show it growing or shrinking, unrelated to anything else. In the lobby on the ground floor a receptionist in a maroon blazer points to a large board showing a tall bar of how many rooms are filled across the whole hotel, with a manager in a suit studying it with folded arms. A thin bracket groups all the rooms and leads down to that board. Warm window light, a cheerful evening mood. Labels: "ONE GUEST" beside a single room's luggage pile, "TOTAL OCCUPANCY" on the lobby board.

key: the teacher tells you that evening
name: ch03_estimate_then_marksheet
alt: A teacher tells a student his rough result on the evening of the exam, and the next morning the official marksheet arrives.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same teenage student in both halves, about sixteen, white school shirt, navy trousers and a backpack. LEFT panel: evening outside a coaching class building, streetlights on, a sky of deep blue. The teacher, a friendly man in his forties with a sleeveless sweater and a register under his arm, leans down and holds his hand flat and wobbles it, saying roughly how the boy did, with a speech bubble showing a fuzzy blurred number "about 80". The boy looks relieved but unsure. RIGHT panel: the next morning at the boy's home, sunlight through the window, his mother pouring tea in the background. The boy holds an official printed marksheet with a stamp and a signature, the exact figure clearly printed and circled, and a small calendar on the wall shows the date one day later than in the left panel. A dotted arrow runs from the fuzzy number in the left bubble to the exact circled figure on the right sheet to show they are close but not identical. Labels: "ESTIMATE" at the top of the left panel, "OFFICIAL" at the top of the right panel.

key: Street view (daily) shows every pothole
name: ch03_map_zoom_pothole_highway
alt: A phone map at three zoom levels: a street full of potholes, a city view showing roads, and a country view where the highway is clear.
scene: Three large phone screens stand side by side in a row from left to right, held by the same hand at the bottom, each showing a generic map app at a different zoom, no logos. LEFT screen: an extreme close-up street view of an Indian road after the monsoon, every pothole visible with puddles, a cow standing at the side, an auto-rickshaw swerving, but the road ahead disappears around a corner so you can't tell where it goes. MIDDLE screen: zoomed out to a whole city, a grid of streets, lakes and flyovers, potholes no longer visible, a thicker road starting to stand out running from bottom left to top right. RIGHT screen: zoomed out to the whole country, one bold highway line clearly running north across the land, with a small blue location dot on it, and no individual streets at all. Between the screens, two small magnifying-glass icons with minus signs show the zooming out. A young commuter in an office shirt peers at the right screen with a satisfied, understanding nod, standing at a bus stop in soft morning light. Labels: "DAILY" under the left screen, "WEEKLY" under the middle screen, and "MONTHLY" under the right screen.

key: In a calm (a range), the sailor keeps
name: ch04_sailboat_wind_vs_calm
alt: A sailboat racing ahead with wind from behind, compared with the same boat in a dead calm where the sailor spins the tiller uselessly and finally drops anchor.
scene: A split-panel seascape divided by a thin vertical line, the same small wooden fishing sailboat with a patched white sail and a lean fisherman in a checked lungi and vest in both halves, off the Konkan coast. LEFT panel: a strong breeze blows from behind, drawn as long curved wind lines; the sail bellies out full, the bow cuts through the water with a white wake trailing far behind, and the fisherman sits relaxed at the tiller with a grin, his hair blown forward. A long straight arrow along the wake shows steady progress toward a distant lighthouse. RIGHT panel: glassy flat water, the sail hanging limp. The same fisherman is frantically yanking the tiller one way and the other, sweat on his brow, as tiny puffs of wind appear and vanish around the boat in little swirls; a tangled loopy dotted line behind the boat shows it going round in circles and getting nowhere. In a small inset at the bottom right, the calm, wiser version of him has thrown a rusty anchor overboard on a rope and sits back with a cup of tea under a towel. Bright sun, sparkling sea on the left, hazy stillness on the right. Labels: "TREND" at the top of the left panel, "RANGE" at the top of the right panel, and "DROP ANCHOR" beside the inset.

key: Someone leaning on a door. A crack
name: ch04_door_crack_vs_wide_open
alt: A thin crack of light under a door convinces nobody in the room, but when the door swings wide open everyone stands up and changes plans.
scene: A two-step scene inside a waiting room of a government office, a row of plastic chairs, a ceiling fan, a wall clock and a closed wooden door at the far end, shown as two panels side by side divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a burly man in a khaki uniform leans his shoulder against the door from the other side, so the door has moved only a hair and a thin sliver of light shows along its edge and under it. Five people waiting on the chairs, a student with a file, an old woman with a cloth bag, a clerk reading a newspaper, a mother with a toddler and a man in a cap, barely glance up; one shrugs. A small magnifying-glass inset shows the tiny crack of light. RIGHT panel: the same door has swung fully open, bright daylight flooding into the room in a wide beam. All five people are now on their feet, gathering their files and bags, the clerk folding his newspaper, the mother lifting the toddler, everyone moving toward the doorway; a big curved arrow shows the door's swing. Lighting: dim and stuffy on the left, bright and decisive on the right. Labels: "SMALL POKE" under the left door, "CLEAR BREAK" under the right door.

key: A queue of buyers all standing exactly
name: ch04_queue_at_price_sign
alt: A crowd of buyers packed exactly at a price sign painted on the floor, while one smart buyer stands a step in front and gets served first.
scene: A bright mid-shot outside a popular sweet shop in an Indian bazaar during a festival sale, glass counters full of colourful mithai, strings of lights and a striped awning. Painted on the pavement in front of the counter is a big yellow line with a price sign on a stand beside it showing a round number. A dense cluster of buyers, uncles in sweaters, aunties with shopping bags, college students, all stand jammed exactly on that yellow line, elbowing and stretching their arms toward the counter, a crowd so tight that nobody moves. Just one step in front of the line, a sharp young woman in a kurta and sling bag stands alone at the counter and is already being handed a box of sweets by the smiling shopkeeper. On the right side, a nervous man has stuck a little red flag into the ground right on the yellow line in the middle of the crowd, and arrows from many pointing fingers in the crowd aim straight at his flag, showing it is the spot everyone is targeting. Midday sun, festive and busy. Labels: "EVERYONE HERE" above the crowd on the line, "ONE STEP AHEAD" above the young woman, and "YOUR STOP" beside the red flag.

key: Two footprints show someone walked here
name: ch04_third_footprint_confirms
alt: Footprints on a wet beach: two prints with a guessed line through them, and a third print landing on the same line to prove it is a real path.
scene: A high-angle view looking down at smooth wet sand on a quiet beach in Puri at dawn, small waves curling in at the top of the picture, a fishing boat pulled up in the far corner. In the foreground two bare footprints sit some distance apart, and a thin dashed line has been drawn through them with a stick, stretching across the sand in both directions, as if guessing where the walker went. A young boy in shorts and a faded T-shirt crouches beside the first print, holding the stick, head tilted, unsure. Further along the dashed line, a third footprint has just landed exactly on it, freshly pressed, with a tiny splash of water; a small check-mark bubble pops above it. Off to the side, a few random prints from crabs and a dog wander about but do not touch the line, to show coincidental marks. In the distance the walker, an elderly fisherman carrying a net over his shoulder, continues along the same line toward the boat. Soft pink dawn light and long shadows. Labels: "TWO POINTS" beside the first two prints, "THIRD TOUCH" above the third print, and "REAL PATH" along the line near the fisherman.

key: A handrail on a staircase. While you
name: ch04_handrail_lean_then_let_go
alt: A climber leans on a staircase handrail while going up, and when his hand breaks through a broken section he steps off the stairs instead of continuing.
scene: A side view of a long outdoor stone staircase climbing up a hillside to a temple, with a metal handrail running diagonally upward along its right side, monkeys sitting on the wall and pilgrims in the distance. The picture shows the same pilgrim, a middle-aged man in a white kurta and a saffron scarf carrying a brass pot, at two moments along the stairs. LOWER LEFT: he climbs steadily, one hand resting on the handrail every time he pauses, and small curved arrows show him dipping slightly to lean on the rail and then pushing on up. UPPER RIGHT: a section of the handrail is rusted and broken, and his hand has just gone straight through the gap, a little burst of rust flakes falling. Instead of trying to keep climbing, he has calmly stepped sideways off the staircase onto a flat landing area with a bench, setting down his pot, while a dotted line shows the long steep drop he would risk if he kept going. A nearby sign post reads a simple arrow pointing off. Clear morning light, a sense of sensible caution. Labels: "TRENDLINE" along the intact handrail, "BREAK" at the broken section, and "STEP OFF" above the landing.

key: Set it too sensitive and it goes off
name: ch04_smoke_alarm_sensitivity_dial
alt: Three kitchens show a smoke alarm set too sensitive ringing at toast, set too dull staying silent in a real fire, and set right with a dial in the middle.
scene: A horizontal strip of three small kitchen scenes side by side, each in a compact Indian apartment kitchen with a gas stove, steel utensils and a window, and each with a round white smoke alarm on the ceiling that has a big visible dial on its side. LEFT: the dial is turned to the far left; a sleepy young man in a vest holds a slice of toast with a single wisp of smoke, while the alarm screams with big jagged sound lines and he covers his ears in annoyance. MIDDLE: the dial is turned to the far right; a frying pan is on fire with real flames climbing the wall and thick smoke, but the alarm sits silent with a small sleeping zzz, and a woman in a nightie runs in from the doorway with a bucket, shocked. RIGHT: the dial is in the middle; normal cooking steam rises from a pressure cooker and the alarm stays quiet, while a small inset below shows the same alarm ringing only when a real flame appears. An older man in a sweater calmly adjusts the dial with a satisfied face. Warm kitchen light throughout. Labels: "TOO SENSITIVE" above the left kitchen, "TOO DULL" above the middle kitchen, and "FILTER" above the right kitchen's dial.

key: A ceiling turned into a floor when you
name: ch04_ceiling_becomes_floor_pendulum
alt: A cut-away two-storey house where a man climbs through to the upper floor and stands on what used to be his ceiling, with a pendulum swinging equally far on both sides of the floorboard.
scene: A cut-away side view of a simple two-storey Indian house, like a dollhouse with the front wall removed, with one thick wooden floorboard line running across the middle that serves as the ceiling of the ground floor and the floor of the upper room. On the ground floor at left, a man in a striped shirt reaches up and presses his palms against that ceiling, unable to get through. On the upper floor at right, the same man has climbed through a trapdoor and now stands comfortably on the same board, which has become his floor, a little rug laid on it. A dashed loop shows a later moment where he falls back through to the ground floor and the board is a ceiling again above his head. Hanging from the very top of the house is a brass clock pendulum whose bob swings across the middle board: the swing reaches as far above the board as it was below it before crossing, shown with two equal measured brackets. A cat watches from the stairs. Warm interior lamplight. Labels: "RESISTANCE" on the board under the man's palms, "SUPPORT" on the board under his feet upstairs, and "SAME DISTANCE" beside the two brackets.

key: A runner slowing down. First they
name: ch04_runner_sprint_jog_walk
alt: A runner climbing a hill road who first drops from a sprint to a jog, then to a walk, and finally stops climbing altogether.
scene: A wide side view of a winding hill road climbing from lower left to upper right through tea gardens near Munnar, misty hills behind. The same runner appears four times along the road like a time-lapse: a young man in a white vest, black shorts and running shoes, with a sweatband. FIRST, low on the left: he sprints hard, knees high, arms pumping, steep speed lines behind him. SECOND, a little higher: he has dropped to a steady jog, breathing harder. THIRD, higher still: he walks with hands on hips up the slope, head down, a water bottle in hand. FOURTH, near the top right: he has stopped climbing altogether and stands on the flat roadside, bent over, with the road ahead still rising unused. Three fan-shaped dotted lines start from the same point at the bottom of the road and get flatter each time, the first steep, the second gentler, the third almost flat, each one broken where the runner slows below it. A tea plucker in a bright saree with a basket on her back watches from the bushes. Soft morning mist and light. Labels: "LINE 1" on the steepest dotted line, "LINE 2" on the middle line, and "LINE 3" on the flattest line.

key: A car on a motorway ramp. Flooring it
name: ch04_motorway_ramp_angles
alt: Three cars on three slopes: one roaring up a too-steep ramp, one cruising on a moderate slope, and one crawling along an almost flat hard shoulder.
scene: A wide, clean side view of an expressway interchange with three separate ramps rising from left to right against a pale sky, each carrying one small car. TOP ramp: very steep, almost like a ski jump; a red hatchback roars up it with the driver gripping the wheel, smoke from the exhaust and sweat on his face, a small fuel gauge inset beside it with the needle plunging, and a crack forming in the ramp ahead showing it can't hold. MIDDLE ramp: a moderate slope at about forty-five degrees, a white sedan cruising smoothly up it, its driver, a calm woman in sunglasses, steering with one hand, a small protractor arc drawn at the base of the ramp. BOTTOM: nearly flat, a tired old scooter with a sack of vegetables on the back crawls along the hard shoulder, its rider in a cap barely moving, with a snail sitting on the kerb going just as fast. Thin arrows show each vehicle's direction and their different steepness. Midday light, highway signs blank except for a small arrow. Labels: "TOO STEEP" above the top ramp, "45 DEGREES" beside the middle ramp's arc, and "TOO FLAT" under the bottom path.

key: the trendline is the left lane marking
name: ch04_lane_markings_channel
alt: A car on a highway seen from above drifts past the right lane marking when speeding up, and later wanders toward the left marking before crossing it.
scene: A top-down aerial view of a straight Indian highway running diagonally from bottom left to top right, one lane picked out with a solid left marking and a dashed right marking. The same small blue car appears several times along the lane like a time-lapse, each copy slightly faded except the latest. In the lower part of the road, the car weaves comfortably between the two markings, touching each in turn. In the middle stretch, the car surges and drifts just past the right marking, with speed lines and a small speedometer inset whose needle jumps up. In the upper stretch, the car no longer reaches the right marking at all and instead drifts closer and closer to the left marking, with a thin dotted path showing it hugging the left edge; at the very top a warning triangle hovers just where it is about to cross the left line. Trucks with painted tails and a bullock cart sit on the shoulder for scale. Bright overhead sun and crisp shadows. Labels: "TRENDLINE" along the left marking, "CHANNEL LINE" along the right marking, and "WATCH HERE" next to the warning triangle.

key: A crowd rushing into a shop at opening
name: ch04_shop_rush_and_exit
alt: A crowd surging into a shop at opening time, then the same crowd streaming back out by closing time, with the shop's clock marking both moments.
scene: A split-panel street view of the same large electronics store in a Mumbai market, divided by a thin vertical line, with a big clock above the shop's entrance. LEFT panel: the clock shows ten in the morning; the shutter has just rolled up and a huge eager crowd of shoppers pushes in through the doors, young men with phones, families, an uncle waving a newspaper advertisement, all leaning forward, motion lines and a big inward arrow into the shop, the shopkeeper behind the counter grinning. A thin rising line drawn above the crowd peaks at the doorway. RIGHT panel: the clock shows evening; the same crowd, now mostly empty-handed and disappointed, streams back out of the doors onto the street, some shaking their heads, one woman checking her receipt and frowning, a big outward arrow leading away from the shop, the shopkeeper now looking worried. The line above them slopes down to end lower than where the morning began. Sunny morning light on the left, orange dusk light with streetlamps switching on at the right. Labels: "HIGH" above the morning rush, "CLOSE" above the evening exit, and "REVERSAL DAY" across the top of both panels.

key: A runner stops and stands still at a
name: ch05_runner_paused_crossroads
alt: A jogger seen from behind stands still at a crossroads, with two ghosted possibilities: turning back home or bending to tie a shoelace and carrying on.
scene: A view from behind and slightly above a jogger standing still at a quiet crossroads on an early morning in a small town, a tea stall with a steaming kettle on one corner, a signpost with blank arrow boards pointing in four directions, and a long road stretching ahead toward a park. The jogger is a man in his forties in a grey track suit and white sports shoes, hands on hips, completely still, his back to the viewer so his face can't be seen. Two faint ghost versions of him branch out like possibilities: on the left, a translucent copy has turned around and is jogging back down the road he came from toward a row of houses, a curved U-turn arrow above it; on the right, another translucent copy bends down to tie a loose shoelace, with a small straight arrow pointing ahead along the original road. A big question-mark bubble floats above the real jogger's head. The tea-stall owner in a vest and lungi watches over his kettle, equally curious. Soft blue-grey morning light with mist. Labels: "REVERSAL" above the U-turn ghost, "CONTINUATION" above the shoelace ghost, and "WAIT" over the real jogger.

key: A climber reaches a ledge (A), rests
name: ch05_climber_ledges_rope_snaps
alt: A rock climber reaches a ledge, rests, climbs higher more slowly, slides back, fails to reach the high ledge, and the rope tied between his two resting points snaps.
scene: A wide side view of a tall rocky cliff face in the Western Ghats, green monsoon moss on the rock, a waterfall in the far background. The same climber, a wiry young man in an orange helmet, grey shirt and harness, appears five times on the cliff like a time-lapse, each marked with a small letter in a circle. At A he hauls himself onto a ledge, triumphant. At B, lower down, he sits resting on a narrow shelf, drinking water. At C he has reached a higher ledge than A, but he is clearly exhausted, chalk bag empty, face strained. At D he has slid back down to a resting shelf about level with B. At E he reaches only to roughly the height of A, well below C, arm stretched, unable to go higher. A horizontal safety rope is tied between pitons at the two resting shelves B and D, running across the cliff; under the climber's final position the rope has just snapped with a jagged break, frayed ends flying, and a long downward arrow shows the fall beginning. A small belayer far below on the ground looks up in alarm. Overcast light, damp and tense. Labels: "HEAD" beside C, "SHOULDERS" spanning A and E, and "NECKLINE" along the rope.

key: A floor that has held twice (B and D)
name: ch05_floor_crack_and_return_look
alt: A man's foot slips through a crack in a wooden floor without falling, later he falls through and stands below it, then climbs back to peer at the hole from underneath.
scene: A cut-away side view of an old wooden-floored godown building, showing an upper floor of planks and the ground-level room beneath, sacks of rice stacked around, dusty light through a high window. Three moments are shown left to right along the floor. LEFT: a worker in a vest and a cloth tied round his head is standing on the upper floor, and one foot has pushed down through a narrow crack between two planks, but his body is still above the floor, his face surprised, a small label tag reads day time. MIDDLE: the planks have given way and the same worker is now standing on the ground below the floor, dust drifting down around him, a wall clock beside him showing evening, and a lantern hanging nearby. RIGHT: the worker has dragged a stool under the hole and climbs up to look at the broken planks from underneath, his head just touching the edge of the hole, before turning away, with a dotted arrow showing him then walking off to the right toward the exit. Warm dusty interior light with shafts of sunlight. Labels: "INTRADAY DIP" under the left moment, "CLOSE BELOW" under the middle moment, and "RETURN MOVE" under the right moment.

key: A ball thrown up past a window ledge
name: ch05_ball_past_ledge_same_distance
alt: A ball tossed up beside a building rises a measured height above a window ledge, then falls back through the ledge by at least that same distance, but not below the ground it started from.
scene: A side view of the front of a three-storey apartment building in a residential colony, with a balcony window ledge on the middle floor, potted tulsi plant and drying clothes on the balcony, and a courtyard at the bottom. A boy of about ten in a school-house T-shirt stands in the courtyard at the bottom left, having just thrown a red rubber ball straight up beside the building. The ball's path is drawn as a tall dotted vertical arc: rising from the courtyard, passing the window ledge, reaching a peak some distance above it, and then falling back down past the ledge again. A bright measuring bracket beside the building shows the distance from the ledge to the peak, and an identical bracket of the same length is copied below the ledge, ending at a small target mark part way down the wall. The falling ball is caught just past that target mark. The courtyard ground at the bottom has a thick line marking it, with a small note that the ball may bounce all the way back there but no lower. An aunty leaning out of the balcony watches with her hand on her cheek. Sunny afternoon light, clear shadows. Labels: "NECKLINE" along the window ledge, "SAME DISTANCE" between the two brackets, and "START FLOOR" on the courtyard line.

key: A ball dropped down a staircase
name: ch05_ball_down_staircase_landings
alt: A ball bouncing down a long staircase with several landings, each landing a place it might stop, and the one next to the calculated target where it actually settles.
scene: A side cut-away view of a tall staircase inside an old office building, drawn as a long zig-zag of flights going down from top left to bottom right, with several wide landings at different heights. A football has been dropped from the top landing and its bouncing path is traced with a dotted line down the stairs. Each landing is a little different and remembered: one has a potted plant, one has a water cooler and a bench where a peon in a khaki uniform sits, one has a notice board, one has a coat rack, so they look like familiar places people stop. A man in a white shirt and tie stands at the top with a clipboard on which he has drawn a red arrow pointing to a particular floor number. Beside the stairs, a thin red dashed horizontal line marks his calculated floor; right next to that line is a broad landing with a bench, and the ball has come to rest on that landing rather than at the exact red line. Small question marks hover at the other landings where the ball paused briefly. Fluorescent office light with a window letting in daylight. Labels: "TARGET" on the red dashed line, "LANDING" beside the bench where the ball rests.

key: A boulder rolls downhill by itself
name: ch05_boulder_down_easy_up_crowd
alt: A boulder rolls downhill on its own with nobody pushing, while on the other side of the hill a large crowd strains to push another boulder up.
scene: A wide side view of a rounded grassy hill in a rural landscape with a mud road and a few huts, divided visually into two slopes by the hilltop in the middle. LEFT slope: a big grey boulder tumbles down by itself, bouncing, with motion lines and puffs of dust, while two goats and a lone shepherd boy simply watch from the side with their hands empty; nobody touches it, and a smooth downward arrow follows it. RIGHT slope: an identical boulder is being pushed up the hill by a large crowd of villagers, men in vests and dhotis, women in sarees tucked up, a few teenagers, all leaning hard into the rock with strained faces, sweat drops flying, some pulling on ropes tied round it. A drummer at the side beats a dhol to keep their rhythm, and more villagers are running in from a nearby hut to join. Musical and effort lines surround the crowd. A small hut on the hilltop marks the dividing point between the two slopes. Bright midday sun, dusty air. Labels: "FALLS ON ITS OWN" on the left slope, "NEEDS A CROWD" on the right slope, and "VOLUME" above the arriving villagers.

key: A face in a mirror: if you see two
name: ch05_mirror_face_symmetry
alt: A face half reflected in a mirror: the visible left side shows two bumps, and the unfinished right side is sketched in dotted lines as their mirror image.
scene: A close-up of a round wall mirror in a simple bathroom with tiled walls and a toothbrush in a steel cup on the shelf. A young woman in her twenties with her hair tied up in a towel leans toward the mirror; we see her face from the side at the left edge of the picture. In the mirror, only the left half of her reflected face is fully drawn and solid, with a small clip and a little curl making two clear bumps along the outline of her head. The right half of the reflection is not yet drawn in: instead, a dotted outline sketches two matching bumps in exactly mirrored positions, and two curved arrows lead from each solid bump across a thin vertical centre line to its dotted twin. A small ruler drawn along the centre line shows the equal distances on both sides. A pencil hovers at the right side of the mirror as if completing the sketch. A small sticky note on the mirror frame shows a simple sketch of a head-and-shoulders outline with only its left half filled in. Soft morning light from a small window. Labels: "WHAT HAS FORMED" over the solid half, "EXPECTED SHAPE" over the dotted half.

key: Buying a house in a neighbourhood
name: ch05_house_deposit_then_cafe
alt: A couple puts a small deposit on a cheap house among run-down homes, then buys a larger one after the first new cafe opens on the street.
scene: A wide street view of an old neighbourhood in a small city that is starting to change, shown as two moments left and right divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT: the street is still shabby, peeling paint, a closed shutter with graffiti, a stray dog asleep, but a single house has fresh scaffolding. A young couple, he in a checked shirt and she in a kurta with a laptop bag, hand a thin envelope of cash to a smiling elderly owner in front of a small faded house with a cheap price sign hanging from its gate. A small coin icon above them shows a modest amount. RIGHT: some months later on the same street, a bright new cafe with fairy lights, outdoor tables and young people sipping coffee has opened, fresh plants line the pavement, and painters are working. The same couple stands in front of a bigger, nicer house with a higher price sign, now handing over a much thicker envelope, holding a set of keys. A dotted arrow runs from the small left envelope to the larger right one. Left lighting is grey and dusty, right lighting warm and sunny. Labels: "SMALL EARLY BET" over the left panel, "BIGGER BET" over the right panel, and "NECKLINE BREAK" beside the new cafe.

key: Someone knocks on a door, gets no answer
name: ch05_knock_then_past_gate
alt: A visitor knocks on a front door, steps back onto the path still waiting, and only truly leaves once he walks past the garden gate.
scene: A side view of a small bungalow with a red front door, a short garden path with potted hibiscus and a low iron garden gate at the left, with the street beyond. The same visitor, a middle-aged man in a pale blue shirt holding a box of sweets, is shown three times along the path like a time-lapse, each copy slightly fainter than the next. FIRST, at the right by the door: he knocks with a raised knuckle, small knock lines on the door, a speech bubble with an ellipsis showing no reply. SECOND, in the middle of the path: he has stepped back a few paces and stands looking up at the windows, still holding the sweets, clearly still waiting. THIRD, at the left: he has walked out through the garden gate onto the street, with the gate swinging shut behind him and a firm arrow pointing away down the road. A dotted line runs vertically through the gate post, the dividing point. A curious neighbour in a nightie peeks over the wall. Warm late-afternoon light. Labels: "STEPS BACK" under the middle figure, "REACTION LOW" at the gate post, and "GONE" under the left figure.

key: Two people pushing a door from opposite
name: ch06_door_push_three_triangles
alt: Three doorways show two people pushing a door from opposite sides: both giving ground equally, one side standing firm while the other edges closer, and the reverse.
scene: A row of three identical wooden double-hinged doors in a long corridor of an old college building, each door shown in a cut-away top-down view so we see a person pushing from each side, divided into three panels. LEFT panel: a buyer in a green T-shirt pushes from below and a seller in a red T-shirt pushes from above; both have taken small steps toward the door, their earlier footprints fading behind them in two converging diagonal rows, a balanced scale icon over the door. MIDDLE panel: the seller in red stands rooted to one spot with his feet planted on a painted line, arms braced, his footprints all on the same flat line, while the buyer in green keeps stepping closer with each push, her footprints rising toward the door; a bulge in the door shows it is about to burst open toward the seller's side, with a bold arrow. RIGHT panel: the mirror case, the buyer stands firm on a flat line and the seller keeps stepping closer, the door bulging the other way with an arrow. Both people in every panel are young students with determined faces. Even fluorescent corridor light. Labels: "SYMMETRICAL" above the left panel, "ASCENDING" above the middle panel, and "DESCENDING" above the right panel.

key: the walls are close enough that the ball
name: ch06_funnel_ball_two_thirds
alt: A ball bouncing inside a large funnel, shooting out of the side two-thirds of the way down, while another ball that reaches the narrow tip just dribbles out.
scene: A large clear glass funnel lies on its side on a workbench in a school science lab, its wide mouth on the left and its narrow spout on the right, with lab stools and a periodic table poster behind. Inside it, a bright orange rubber ball's path is drawn as a dotted zig-zag line: wide bounces near the open mouth, getting shorter and quicker as the walls close in. About two-thirds of the way along, the funnel has a cut opening in its side, and the ball shoots out through it with strong motion lines, a burst of energy and a long arrow continuing to the right. Below, a second faded copy of the funnel shows the alternative: a grey ball has rolled all the way to the narrow tip and simply dribbles out of the spout, dropping limply onto the bench with a tiny plop and a sad little wobble line. A ruler lies along the funnel with marks at one-third and two-thirds. A curious teenage student in a lab coat and goggles leans in on the left watching, while a teacher with a pointer stands at the right. Bright lab lighting. Labels: "TWO-THIRDS" at the side opening, "APEX" at the tip of the lower funnel.

key: An auction room where the bids have
name: ch06_auction_quiet_then_jump
alt: An auction room falls silent with paddles down, then one bidder jumps the price and half the room starts bidding; a small inset shows the alternative where nobody follows.
scene: A two-part interior scene of a cattle and farm-equipment auction held in a big shed in Punjab, wooden benches, a raised platform with a shiny red tractor on display, a chalkboard showing the current bid. LEFT half: the room has gone quiet; farmers in turbans and woollen shawls sit with their numbered paddles resting on their knees, some yawning, one checking his phone, the auctioneer in a waistcoat leaning on his lectern, and small sound waves above the crowd fading to nothing. RIGHT half: one young farmer in a bright yellow turban has leapt to his feet and thrust his paddle high with a shout, a big upward jump arrow on the chalkboard beside a higher figure, and suddenly half the room is raising paddles again, people turning to look, sound lines and excitement filling the space. In a small inset at the bottom right corner, an alternative ending: the young farmer stands alone with his paddle up, everyone else still seated, and the auctioneer has rubbed the chalkboard back down to the old figure. Dusty shafts of sunlight through the shed roof. Labels: "QUIET" over the left half, "BREAKOUT" over the right half, and "NO FOLLOW" beside the inset.

key: A spring squeezed between two hands
name: ch06_spring_base_jump
alt: A coiled spring squeezed between two hands, with the width of the hands at the start measured and copied above the spring to show how far it should jump when released.
scene: A close-up on a wooden workshop table in a small mechanic's shop, tools hanging on a pegboard behind. On the left, two strong hands of a mechanic with grease on the knuckles start far apart, gripping a large steel coil spring, and a bright bracket underneath measures that starting width. Moving right in the same picture, the hands have closed in, squeezing the spring tight between them, the coils bunched together and visibly straining, small tension lines around it. On the far right, the hands have let go and the spring is leaping upward off the table with strong motion lines; the same bracket from the starting width is copied vertically above the release point, showing the minimum height it is expected to reach, with the spring just touching its top. A thin, faint diagonal line rises from the bottom of the squeeze at the same slope as the rising lower hand, offering a second guess for how high it might go. The mechanic, a man in his fifties with a moustache and blue overalls, watches with a slight smile. Warm workshop light. Labels: "BASE" on the starting bracket, "TARGET" at the top of the copied bracket.

key: A goalkeeper who never leaves the goal
name: ch06_goalkeeper_attacks_closer
alt: A goalkeeper holds his line while attackers start each new attack closer to the goal, until one shot goes in.
scene: A high-angle view of a school football pitch with chalk lines, a goal at the bottom of the picture and a small crowd of students sitting on a low wall. The goalkeeper, a stocky boy in a green jersey and gloves, stands planted on the goal line, which is drawn as a thick flat white line, and he never moves forward off it. Coming from the top of the pitch toward him are several attacks shown as numbered dotted paths of attackers in red jerseys. Each attack starts from a point a little closer to the goal than the last, and after each attack the attackers retreat less far than before, so the turning points form a downward-sloping dotted line from upper left toward the goal. The goalkeeper's diving saves are shown as small burst marks on the first three attacks. On the latest attack, the ball flies past his fingertips into the net, the net bulging with motion lines, a striker celebrating. A teacher with a whistle watches from the sideline. Bright afternoon sun and long shadows. Labels: "FLAT FLOOR" along the goal line, "LOWER HIGHS" along the dotted line of attack starts, and "BREAK" at the net.

key: A stop at a traffic light and a stop
name: ch06_traffic_light_vs_lunch_stop
alt: The same family car is shown pausing briefly at a traffic light and pausing for a long lunch at a highway dhaba, with clocks showing the difference in time.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same small silver family car with a roof carrier full of bags, heading the same direction to the right. LEFT panel: the car waits at a red traffic signal at a busy city crossing, the father at the wheel tapping his fingers, the mother beside him checking a map on her phone, two kids in the back, scooters and autos around them; a small stopwatch inset shows just under a minute. A short arrow ahead shows they will carry straight on. RIGHT panel: the car is parked outside a roadside highway dhaba with charpoy beds, steel plates of food and a tandoor smoking; the family sits on a charpoy eating rotis and dal, the kids drinking lassi, the father stretching. A wall clock at the dhaba shows a much longer time has passed, about an hour, and the same short arrow ahead shows they will carry on in the same direction. A road sign in both panels points the same way. Midday light on the left, warm lazy afternoon light on the right. Labels: "SHORT PAUSE" over the left panel, "LONG PAUSE" over the right panel.

key: An argument in a crowd that gets louder
name: ch06_argument_growing_crowd
alt: A street argument that grows louder with each round as more people join, the circle widening and nobody in charge.
scene: A high-angle view of a crowded street corner near a vegetable market, carts of tomatoes and onions, a parked auto-rickshaw and a lamp post. At the centre, a quarrel that started between two men, a vendor in a vest and a customer in a shirt, has spread outward in widening rings. The innermost ring has two people shouting; the next ring has six people, more angry; the outer ring has a dozen or more, waving arms, pointing, some standing on a cart to shout louder. Speech bubbles grow bigger with each ring, from small jagged ones in the centre to huge jagged ones at the edge, each containing only exclamation marks. Two diverging dotted lines spread out from the centre like a megaphone, showing the swings getting wider each round. A lone traffic policeman in khaki stands at the edge scratching his head, clearly not in control, his whistle dangling. A dropped basket of tomatoes rolls in the foreground. Hot, harsh midday light. Labels: "BIGGER EACH ROUND" along the dotted lines, "NOBODY IN CHARGE" above the policeman.

key: a ball bouncing down a narrowing
name: ch06_wedge_narrowing_staircase
alt: A ball bouncing down a staircase whose steps get smaller and closer together, losing energy; beside it the upside-down version where each push up gains less.
scene: A clean side-view illustration of two unusual staircases side by side against a plain wall in a modern building lobby. LEFT staircase: it goes down from upper left to lower right, but each step is smaller than the one before, the flights shrinking and the treads closer together, so the whole staircase narrows to a point. A blue ball bounces down it, its dotted path showing tall bounces at the top that become short, quick little hops near the bottom, with fading motion lines and a little sweat drop on the ball to show it is running out of energy. Two converging lines are drawn along the step edges, top and bottom. RIGHT staircase: the mirror image going up from lower left to upper right, also narrowing, with a small boy in a school uniform pushing a heavy box up it; each push moves the box only a shorter distance than the last, little arrows shrinking in size, his face more tired at each step. A security guard at a desk in the lobby watches with mild interest. Even indoor daylight. Labels: "FALLING WEDGE" over the left staircase, "RISING WEDGE" over the right staircase.

key: A ball bouncing between the floor and
name: ch06_ball_room_ceiling_breakout
alt: A ball bouncing between the floor and ceiling of a room, then bursting through the ceiling into the room above, where people happily stand on that old ceiling.
scene: A cut-away side view of a two-storey building like a dollhouse with the front wall removed. In the lower room, a plain rectangular hall with a tiled floor, a yellow ball bounces back and forth between the floor and the ceiling, its path drawn as a long dotted zig-zag touching both surfaces many times. A measuring tape hangs on the wall showing the height of the room, and the same height is copied above the ceiling as a dotted bracket into the upper room. At the right side of the lower room the ball has smashed up through the ceiling, a hole with splintered edges and a burst of plaster, and it now flies into the upper room, reaching about the top of the copied bracket. In the upper room, a family has set down a carpet and is happily standing and sitting on what was the ceiling of the lower room, a grandmother on a chair, a boy playing on the floor, everyone treating it as a solid floor. Several neighbours watched the ceiling from below earlier and are now upstairs too. Warm interior light. Labels: "ROOM HEIGHT" beside the tape, "TARGET" at the top of the copied bracket, and "CEILING BECOMES FLOOR" on the upper floor.

key: OBV is a bank balance. Every up day
name: ch07_obv_passbook_balance
alt: A bank passbook where up days are deposits and down days are withdrawals, and the balance at the newest price high is lower than at the previous high.
scene: A close-up over the shoulder of a retired schoolteacher, a man in his sixties with white hair, spectacles and a half-sleeve shirt, sitting at a bank counter with an old-fashioned printed passbook open in front of him, a pen and a steel tumbler of water beside it. The passbook has neat rows: green rows marked with a small up-arrow are deposits, red rows with a small down-arrow are withdrawals, and a running balance column on the right. Two rows are highlighted with yellow marker, each with a small mountain-peak icon beside it showing a new high in price; the later peak icon is drawn taller than the earlier one, but the balance written next to the later peak is clearly smaller than the balance next to the earlier peak, and a red circle surrounds the smaller figure. Above the passbook a thought bubble from the teacher shows a shiny new car parked on top of a stack of credit-card slips, meaning the rally is being bought on credit. A bank clerk in a blue saree behind the glass counter raises an eyebrow. Fluorescent bank lighting, a ceiling fan turning slowly. Labels: "DEPOSIT" beside a green row, "WITHDRAWAL" beside a red row, and "LOWER BALANCE" beside the red-circled figure.

key: Rising OI is new players walking onto
name: ch07_players_on_and_off_field
alt: On one side of a cricket ground fresh players stream onto the field and the game surges; on the other, players walk off one by one until the field is almost empty.
scene: A wide high-angle view of a local cricket maidan divided by a thin vertical line into two scenes of the same ground. LEFT side: a gate in the boundary fence is open and a steady stream of new players in white clothes and caps jogs onto the field carrying bats and kit bags, waving and stretching, with a big inward arrow through the gate; the game on the pitch is lively, the ball flying, fielders diving, and a big fuel can icon sits beside the scoreboard showing it is full. RIGHT side: the same gate, but now players are walking off the field one by one with their kit bags over their shoulders, heads down, toward a parked bus; a big outward arrow leads through the gate. Only three players are left on the field, standing around, and the fuel can icon beside this scoreboard is nearly empty, with the last player shown stepping through the gate. Spectators in the stands on the left cheer while those on the right are packing up their tiffin boxes. Late-afternoon light, long shadows. Labels: "RISING OPEN INTEREST" over the left side, "FALLING OPEN INTEREST" over the right side.

key: Splicing film shot on different cameras
name: ch08_splicing_film_reels
alt: A film editor splicing reels from different cameras four ways: at the end of each reel with a jump, earlier before the shaky end, one camera per year, or recoloured to match.
scene: An overhead view of a cluttered old film editor's desk in a small studio in Chennai, a lamp, a cup of filter coffee, film canisters stacked to one side. A grey-haired editor in a striped shirt with a magnifying loupe on a cord around his neck holds a pair of splicing scissors over a lightbox. Across the lightbox, four horizontal strips of film run left to right, one under the other, each made by joining frames from several reels in slightly different colours. TOP strip: frames are joined right at the last frame of each reel, and at every join the picture jumps sharply up or down, marked with a small jagged lightning icon. SECOND strip: joins are made a few frames earlier, before the blurry, shaky final frames of each reel, which lie cut off in a little pile. THIRD strip: all frames in each section come from one reel only, a single colour per year, with a small calendar icon. BOTTOM strip: the older frames have been tinted so their colours match the newer reel at every join, giving a perfectly smooth strip, but a small inset shows an original frame beside its recoloured copy, clearly different. Warm lamp light. Labels: "JUMPS" beside the top strip, "ROLL EARLY" beside the second strip, and "ADJUSTED" beside the bottom strip.

key: A 20-day average is a photo made from
name: ch09_blended_photo_twenty_days
alt: Twenty daily photos of a street stacked into one blended picture whose middle frame is ten days old, while the live street has already moved on.
scene: A wide scene in a small photo studio in a market lane, with a window looking out onto the actual street. On a long table on the left, twenty small printed photos of the same street corner are fanned out in a row like playing cards, each one dated with a tiny day number, showing slight changes: a fruit cart that moves, a building being painted from blue to yellow, a banner going up. A young photographer with curly hair and a camera strap around his neck slides them into a stack, and from the stack a single semi-transparent blended photo rises up into a frame on an easel in the middle; in it the building looks half blue and half yellow and the fruit cart is a ghostly blur. A bracket under the fan of photos marks the middle one with a pin, and a dotted arrow links that middle photo to the blended picture. Through the window on the right, the real street today shows the building fully yellow and the banner already up, clearly ahead of the blended photo. An old customer in a cap compares the framed photo with the window and frowns. Soft studio light, bright daylight outside. Labels: "20 DAYS" above the fan of photos, "10 DAYS OLD" at the pinned middle photo, and "TODAY" on the window.

key: The high/low band is a corridor
name: ch09_corridor_step_outside
alt: A man pacing inside a hotel corridor where nothing happens, and stepping out through a door at either end that means a real move.
scene: A long, straight hotel corridor seen from a slightly raised angle, with patterned carpet, wall lamps, numbered room doors on both sides and an exit door at each end. A restless man in a dressing gown and slippers, holding a cup of tea, paces back and forth inside the corridor; his path is drawn as a loopy dotted line that wanders from wall to wall but never leaves the corridor, with small sleepy zzz marks along it to show nothing is happening. The ceiling of the corridor is outlined in a thin blue line along the top, and the floor edge in a thin orange line along the bottom. At the far right end, a ghost version of the man has stepped out through an exit door onto a sunny rooftop terrace, with a strong upward arrow. At the far left end, another ghost version has gone down through a door to a dim stairwell going below, with a strong downward arrow. A housekeeper with a trolley watches him pacing with a bored look. Warm yellow indoor light in the corridor, bright light at the right exit and shadowy light at the left exit. Labels: "NOTHING HAPPENED" in the middle of the corridor, "STRONGER" at the right exit, and "WEAKER" at the left exit.

key: a sprinter (fast MA) and a marathoner
name: ch09_sprinter_overtakes_marathoner
alt: A sprinter and a marathoner on the same track: the sprinter overtakes after several fast laps, and later the marathoner takes the lead back.
scene: A wide aerial view of an oval running track at a city stadium, lanes painted in white, a scoreboard and a small crowd on the concrete steps. Two runners share the inner lane. The sprinter is a lean young man in a bright orange vest, quick and jumpy, taking short bursts; the marathoner is an older, steady woman in a navy vest with a calm pace and a headband. Their positions are shown three times around the track like a time-lapse. FIRST, on the left bend: the marathoner is ahead and the sprinter is behind. SECOND, along the top straight: after several consecutive quick laps, shown by three small lap tally marks beside him, the sprinter draws level and then overtakes, a small up-arrow over the crossing point. THIRD, on the right bend: the sprinter has tired and slowed, and the marathoner steadily retakes the lead, a small down-arrow over that crossing. An inset near the bottom shows a single stumble by the sprinter on one lap that does not get him past her, with a tiny cross. A coach with a stopwatch watches from the infield. Late-afternoon sun with long shadows. Labels: "FAST" over the sprinter, "SLOW" over the marathoner, and "CROSSOVER" at the overtaking point.

key: The envelope marks how far the band
name: ch09_rubber_band_envelope_snap
alt: A rubber band anchored to a peg is pulled further and further, and past a marked limit it is taut and about to snap back toward the peg.
scene: A close-up on a wooden school desk with a geometry box, a ruler and pencil shavings. A brass drawing pin is pressed into the middle of the desk, and a thick red rubber band is looped around it. A boy of about twelve in a white school shirt with a loosened tie pulls the far end of the band with one finger to the right, and three positions of his finger are shown, each a little further out. At the first two positions the band is relaxed and slightly loose. Two faint pencil lines are drawn on the desk on either side of the pin, parallel to each other, marking how far the band normally stretches. At the third position, the boy's finger has pulled the band beyond the right pencil line: the band is very thin and tight, quivering lines around it, and a curved arrow points back toward the pin, showing it is about to snap back. His friend at the next desk winces with one eye shut, expecting the sting. Classroom daylight from a window, a blackboard softly blurred behind. Labels: "AVERAGE" beside the pin, "ENVELOPE" along the pencil lines, and "SNAP BACK" beside the curved arrow.

key: The bands are the walls of a tunnel
name: ch09_tunnel_walls_squeeze
alt: A tunnel whose walls widen when a noisy crowd pushes through and squeeze tight when it is quiet, compressing a spring that bursts out at the end.
scene: A side cut-away view of a long flexible tunnel, like a giant soft fabric tube held open by hoops, running from left to right across a fairground at dusk. On the left, a noisy crowd of children and adults with balloons and whistles is jostling inside the tunnel, pushing on its walls, and the walls have bulged far apart, with sound lines and outward arrows. In the middle section the crowd has thinned to one quiet person tiptoeing, and the tunnel walls have squeezed in tightly around him, almost touching his shoulders, with inward arrows. In that narrow squeezed stretch a big coiled spring lies along the floor, pressed flatter and flatter by the walls, small tension lines showing it compressed. At the right end of the tunnel the spring has burst free and is shooting out of the opening with strong motion lines, scattering confetti, while a fairground attendant in a cap jumps back in surprise. Coloured fairground lights glow along the hoops; the sky is purple. Labels: "LOUD MARKET" over the wide section, "SQUEEZE" over the narrow section, and "BREAKOUT" at the right opening.

key: A string pulled between two points
name: ch09_string_straight_vs_zigzag
alt: Two pieces of string between the same two pins: one pulled straight so its length equals the distance, the other zig-zagging so it uses lots of string for little distance.
scene: A top-down view of a cork notice board in a tailor's shop, with spools of thread, a measuring tape and scissors scattered around its frame. Two pairs of brass pins are pressed into the board, each pair the same distance apart, one pair in the upper half and one pair in the lower half. In the UPPER half, a red thread is pulled tight and perfectly straight between its pins, and a measuring tape laid alongside shows the thread's length equals the distance exactly, with a small checkmark and a speedy running-shoe icon beside it. In the LOWER half, a blue thread runs between its pins but zig-zags back and forth wildly across the board, looped around many extra pins, using a huge length of thread to cover the same short distance; the leftover length is coiled in a big tangle, and a small snail icon sits beside it to show the average nearly freezes. A tailor, an older man with a measuring tape around his neck and reading glasses on his nose, holds the end of the blue thread with a puzzled expression. Warm shop light. Labels: "TREND" by the straight thread, "CHOP" by the zig-zag thread, and "EFFICIENCY" across the top of the board.

key: An oscillator is a speedometer with
name: ch10_compass_vs_speedometer
alt: A car dashboard with a compass and a speedometer: on the highway the compass shows direction, in a car park the compass spins while the speedometer flags hitting the end of the lot.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing the view from the driver's seat of the same small car, with a dashboard holding two big round instruments: a magnetic compass on the left and a speedometer with a red zone on the right. LEFT panel: through the windscreen, an open highway runs straight toward distant hills; the compass needle points steadily ahead with a firm arrow, while the speedometer sits calmly in its normal range. The driver, a woman in her thirties with a dupatta and sunglasses, steers relaxed. RIGHT panel: through the windscreen, a cramped multi-storey car park with concrete pillars, painted bay lines and a wall at the end very close ahead. The compass needle is spinning in circles, drawn with a blur and circular arrows and a small question mark. The speedometer needle has flicked into the red zone as the car nears the end wall, and a little warning light glows. The same driver now looks alert, foot moving to the brake, a parking attendant in uniform waving his arms at the wall. Bright sunlight on the left, dim fluorescent light on the right. Labels: "MOVING AVERAGE" under the compass, "OSCILLATOR" under the speedometer, and "END OF THE LOT" on the car park wall.

key: momentum is how far the car travelled
name: ch10_car_far_but_barely_moving
alt: A car far along a highway barely creeping forward, compared with another car near the start that is speeding, showing position and recent speed are different things.
scene: A long side view of a highway stretching from left to right across the whole picture, with kilometre stones along the roadside painted in yellow and white showing increasing numbers, and paddy fields and palm trees behind. Near the far right end of the road, at a high kilometre stone, a boxy old black-and-yellow taxi with a roof rack is barely moving, creeping along at walking pace behind a herd of buffaloes crossing the road; its driver leans out of the window resting his chin on his hand, bored. A short bracket under it measures only a tiny distance covered over the last ten days, drawn as a little calendar icon with a very short arrow. Near the left start of the road, at a low kilometre stone, a bright red hatchback is speeding with motion lines and a long bracket beneath it showing a large distance covered in the last ten days, again with a calendar icon and a long arrow. A boy selling coconuts at a roadside stall in the middle looks from one car to the other. Bright afternoon light, heat haze on the road. Labels: "HIGH PRICE" above the far taxi, "MOMENTUM NEAR ZERO" beside its short bracket, and "STRONG MOMENTUM" beside the red car's long bracket.

key: A bus stop where buses go both ways
name: ch10_bus_stop_wrong_side
alt: At a two-way bus stop a commuter checks which way the road runs before boarding, while another who jumps on every bus ends up across town in the wrong place.
scene: A street-level view of a busy two-way road in Bengaluru with a bus shelter on each side and a painted median between them. Buses arrive on both sides at the same moment, one heading left toward a distant cluster of office towers and one heading right toward a far-away industrial area with chimneys. A large arrow painted along the road and a signboard over the left lane point toward the office towers, the direction the trend is going. On the near pavement, a careful office worker in a blue shirt with an ID badge and lunch bag checks his watch and the direction arrow before stepping onto the bus going toward the office towers, a small tick above his head. In a separate inset bubble at the top right, a hasty young man with a backpack is shown jumping onto every bus that pulls in, and ends up standing alone in a dusty field near the chimneys, scratching his head with a confused expression and a small cross over him. A conductor leaning out of a bus door blows a whistle. Morning traffic light, autos and scooters around. Labels: "ZERO CROSS" over the arriving buses, "TREND" on the direction arrow, and "WRONG SIDE OF TOWN" in the inset.

key: A high-water mark painted on a river
name: ch10_river_flood_marks_repainted
alt: Painted high-water marks on an old river wall, with a man repainting new marks at a different height after the river changed course.
scene: A side view of an old stone river wall along a ghat in a north Indian town, stone steps leading down to the water, a small temple with a flag at the top of the steps and boats tied below. Painted on the wall is a vertical scale of horizontal lines in white with small year numbers beside some of them, each marking how high past floods reached, the highest mark well above today's water level. On the left part of the wall, the water is calm and low, far below the marks, with a few children splashing safely. On the right part of the wall, the river now flows along a slightly different course, shown by a curved bank and an old dry channel full of grass, and a workman in a vest and lungi stands on a bamboo ladder with a paint bucket and brush, painting a fresh set of marks at a different height while the old faded marks beside them are crossed out with thin lines. An elderly boatman sitting on the steps points at the new marks, explaining to a curious young woman with a notebook. Morning light reflecting off the water. Labels: "PAST LEVELS" beside the old marks, "REPAINT" beside the workman's fresh marks.

key: A high jumper who clears 2.10 m
name: ch10_high_jumper_tiring
alt: A high jumper clears a high bar, then clears a slightly lower one, then knocks off a warm-up bar she had cleared in between.
scene: A wide view of a high-jump area at a college athletics meet, a foam landing mat, two upright stands with a crossbar, and a few officials in white caps sitting at a small table with a clipboard. The same athlete, a tall young woman in a maroon vest and shorts with her hair in a tight bun, is shown three times from left to right like a sequence. LEFT: she arches cleanly over a high bar with a small tag reading "2.10", the bar staying perfectly still, a small tick above her and an official clapping. MIDDLE: on the next attempt the bar has been set slightly lower, tagged "2.05", and she just scrapes over it, her heel brushing the bar, which wobbles but stays. RIGHT: on a lower warm-up height that she had cleared easily between attempts, she clips the bar and it falls off the stands onto the mat, her face tired and frustrated, sweat on her forehead. A thin dotted line connects the tops of her three jumps, sloping down to the right. Behind them a scoreboard still shows the meet's best height rising, implying the price inches up while she tires. Afternoon sunlight, long shadows on the grass. Labels: "WEAKER PUSH" above the middle jump, "TIRING" above the right jump.

key: A car climbing a hill. The car is still
name: ch10_car_hill_lower_revs
alt: A car reaches a higher point on a ghat road than before, but its rev counter shows lower revs than on the previous climb.
scene: A side view of a winding ghat road with hairpin bends climbing a forested mountain, with two climbs of the same small white car shown along it. On the lower hairpin to the left, the car charges up the slope, exhaust puffing, and a big circular rev-counter inset floats above it with the needle high near the red line. On the upper hairpin to the right, the same car has reached an even higher point on the mountain, a little flag on a stone marker showing the new height, but its rev-counter inset shows the needle noticeably lower than on the first climb, the engine sounding weak with a small wheezing puff from the bonnet. A thin dotted line rising from the first car to the second shows higher height, while a thin dotted line between the two rev needles slopes down. The driver, a middle-aged man in a checked shirt, grips the wheel and glances anxiously at the dashboard. Monkeys sit on the parapet wall, and mist drifts through the trees. Cool morning light. Labels: "HIGHER HIGH" beside the upper car, "LOWER REVS" between the two rev counters, and "DIVERGENCE" across the top.

key: A lift in a 14-floor building whose
name: ch10_lift_floors_shifting
alt: A lift indicator in a building where the ground floor and top floor are set by the lowest and highest prices of the last fourteen days, with today's stop near the roof.
scene: A cut-away front view of a slim fourteen-storey apartment building with a glass lift shaft running up its centre. The floors are numbered with small plates on the left side. The ground floor slab is painted orange and labelled with a small calendar icon showing it was set by the lowest day, and the rooftop slab is painted blue with a calendar icon showing the highest day; dotted ghost outlines just above and below the building show that both slabs shift up and down as days pass, like the building stretching. Inside the glass lift, a cheerful lift operator, an older man in a grey uniform and cap, sits on a stool beside the control panel, which has a big round dial reading "90". The lift car has stopped near the top floor, a resident with a newspaper stepping out onto a terrace with potted plants.
