A bright arrow on the side measures the lift's height as a share of the whole building, from ground to roof. A crow sits on the water tank on the roof. Clear afternoon light. Labels: "LOWEST LOW" on the ground floor slab, "HIGHEST HIGH" on the roof slab, and "PERCENT K" beside the lift dial.

key: A plane on take-off is always at
name: ch10_plane_takeoff_vs_cruise
alt: A plane climbing steeply at take-off with the climb gauge at maximum looks normal, while the same gauge at maximum two hours into the flight worries the pilot.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing a passenger jet with a large inset of its cockpit climb gauge, and the same calm pilot, a woman in her forties with a headset and uniform. LEFT panel: the plane is lifting off a runway at sunrise, nose pointed up steeply, the airport tower and terminal below, a little clock icon showing zero minutes into the flight. The climb gauge inset has its needle pinned at maximum climb, and the pilot sips coffee, relaxed, with a small tick mark beside her. RIGHT panel: the plane is high above fluffy clouds at a level cruising height, the sun bright, a clock icon showing two hours into the flight. The same climb gauge inset again shows the needle pinned at maximum, and now the pilot leans forward frowning, tapping the gauge, while the co-pilot points at it with a worried look and a small warning triangle glows. Passengers' windows below show people asleep, unaware. Soft dawn light on the left, crisp midday light on the right. Labels: "NORMAL AT START" over the left panel, "MEANS SOMETHING" over the right panel.

key: Braking before a red light
name: ch10_foot_off_accelerator_first
alt: A driver's foot moves from the accelerator to the brake before the car stops at a red light, shown as two moments on the road.
scene: A side view of a city road approaching a traffic signal, with the light turning red at the right edge, zebra crossing painted on the road and pedestrians waiting with umbrellas. The same small blue car is shown twice, with a cut-away inset of the driver's footwell under each. FIRST, on the left, still some distance from the signal: the inset shows the driver's foot in a black office shoe lifting off the accelerator pedal and moving across to hover over the brake, a curved arrow showing the shift, while the car still rolls forward with light motion lines. SECOND, on the right, at the stop line: the car has come to a complete halt, the inset showing the foot pressed on the brake, brake lights glowing red. A dotted line connects the two moments, showing the first comes well before the second. A small faded ghost of the car reversing backward appears at the very right edge, crossed out with a thin line, to show that lifting your foot doesn't mean you are about to go backwards. A traffic policeman in white gloves stands at the junction. Evening light with headlights on. Labels: "HISTOGRAM TURN" over the first moment, "CROSSOVER" over the second moment.

key: Betting against a stampede is only
name: ch10_herd_tourists_vs_farmers
alt: A herd of cattle that has stopped growing, with nervous tourists in front who might scatter and calm farmers who actually own the cattle standing their ground.
scene: A wide view of a dusty open plain at a rural cattle fair in Rajasthan, colourful tents and camels in the background, the sky slightly hazy. A large herd of cattle with painted horns has been running and has just slowed to a halt in a dusty cloud, and a gate at the edge of the field has been closed so no more animals are joining, a small closed-padlock icon on it. Two groups of people stand at the front edge of the herd. On the left, a cluster of nervous tourists in sun hats, cameras and sunglasses, clutching each other, one dropping a water bottle, ready to run at the slightest move, with little trembling lines around them. On the right, a group of calm local farmers in large colourful turbans and white dhotis hold sticks and ropes tied to their own cattle, standing firm and chatting, clearly the owners, unbothered. A thin bracket over the tourists and a small target icon shows they are the ones a contrarian would bet on scattering. A boy with a flute sits on a cart watching. Golden late-afternoon light through dust. Labels: "HERD STOPPED GROWING" over the closed gate, "SPECULATORS" over the tourists, and "HEDGERS" over the farmers.

key: Four weather stations measuring the
name: ch10_four_weather_stations
alt: Four separate weather stations around a coastline all register the same storm at an extreme reading, making the signal more trustworthy than any single gauge.
scene: A high bird's-eye view of a curved coastline with a big swirling storm cloud spiralling over the sea, heavy rain bands reaching toward the land. Spread along the coast and inland are four small weather stations: one on a lighthouse, one on a hilltop with a wind vane, one on the roof of a school and one in a farm field, each with its own dial on a pole. All four dials have their needles swung into the same red extreme zone, and four dotted lines lead from the stations to a single small control room in the bottom right corner. Inside that control room, seen through a window, a weather officer in a white shirt and spectacles studies four matching readings pinned on a board and nods confidently. In a small inset on the left, only one station is showing the extreme reading while the other three are normal, and the officer there shrugs with a question mark, unconvinced. Dramatic stormy light with patches of sun breaking through near the control room. Labels: "ONE READING" in the inset, "SEVERAL AGREE" on the control room board.

key: Big ruler + big push = a calm sketch
name: ch11_coarse_vs_fine_sketch
alt: Two artists sketch the same mountain ridge: one with a coarse ruler and heavy push producing a calm outline, the other with a fine ruler producing a detailed jagged drawing.
scene: A wide outdoor scene on a hill viewpoint overlooking a jagged Himalayan ridge in the distance, prayer flags fluttering on a rope at the edge. Two art students sit side by side on folding stools with sketchboards on easels, both drawing the same ridge. On the LEFT, a calm older student in a woollen cap and shawl uses a large wooden ruler marked only in big, widely spaced notches, and his pencil only moves when the line changes by a full notch; his sketch shows a smooth, simple outline of the ridge with just three or four broad rises and falls, and a little steady pencil-pushing arrow shows he needs a strong push before turning direction. On the RIGHT, a young energetic student in a bright puffer jacket uses a small metal ruler with fine millimetre marks, and her sketch is full of tiny peaks, notches and wiggles, every rock visible, her pencil flicking back and forth with many small arrows. A small inset between the boards shows close-ups of the two rulers side by side. A tea seller with a kettle stands behind them, comparing the drawings with amusement. Crisp mountain light, clear blue sky. Labels: "BIG BOX" above the left board, "SMALL BOX" above the right board.

key: A daily high and low are two snapshots
name: ch11_snapshots_timestamps_torn
alt: Two photographs of a kite at its highest and lowest point of the day with their date stamps torn off, and the same chart sketch whichever order they are placed in.
scene: A close-up of a wooden table in a sunny verandah during the kite festival season in Ahmedabad, with spools of manja thread and a pile of colourful paper kites to one side. A teenage boy in a festive kurta and a cap holds two square photographs, one in each hand. The left photo shows a red kite high in the sky at its highest point of the day; the right photo shows the same kite dipping low near a rooftop at its lowest point. The bottom strip of each photo, where the time stamp would be, has been torn off, and the torn strips lie crumpled on the table with question marks. On the table in front of him, two identical small notebook sketches are placed side by side: in one he has laid the high photo first and the low photo second, in the other the low first and the high second, and both sketches show exactly the same single tall column of marks, with an equals sign between them. His little sister leans on the table watching, chin on her hands. Bright winter sunshine and kites dotting the sky outside. Labels: "HIGH" on the left photo, "LOW" on the right photo, and "SAME CHART" over the equals sign.

key: A ramp laid at a fixed slope under the
name: ch11_ramp_speed_limit
alt: A walker climbs faster than a fixed-slope ramp rising beneath him, until he slows and drops below the ramp's edge.
scene: A side view of a long concrete ramp at a fixed slope, the kind used for wheelchairs and luggage trolleys at a railway station, rising from the bottom left to the top right of the picture with a painted yellow edge and a small sign showing its angle. Above the ramp, a man in his thirties in a kurta and carrying a suitcase walks up a separate set of wooden steps that climb faster than the ramp, so his path stays above the ramp's yellow edge for most of the picture, with an upward arrow and a speed-line effect. Several small markers along his path show him gaining height quickly. Toward the right, he slows down, sets the suitcase on the ground and wipes his forehead, and his next few steps drop downward in a column of small circles, falling through and below the yellow edge of the ramp, with a small red flag where he crosses. A railway porter in a red shirt with a brass badge on his arm leans on a trolley at the top, watching and shaking his head. A train is parked at a platform in the background. Afternoon light under the station's tin roof. Labels: "FIXED SLOPE" along the ramp, "FALLS THROUGH" at the red flag.

key: The first subject is the alphabet
name: ch12_alphabet_then_words
alt: A student first copies a new alphabet onto a slate, and next to it learns to read whole words from cards.
scene: A warm classroom scene in an evening language class held in a community hall, with a blackboard, a ceiling fan and a few rows of desks. On the LEFT side, an eager middle-aged learner, a man in a half-sleeve shirt with reading glasses pushed up on his head, sits at a desk copying unfamiliar letters onto a black slate with chalk, each letter shaped like a small candle body with a wick above and below, in white and dark versions, forming a row like an alphabet; an alphabet chart of these candle letters hangs on the wall behind him. On the RIGHT side, a young woman in a kurta with a notebook holds up flash cards from a box, each card showing two or three candle letters arranged together, and above each card a speech bubble gives the word it spells as a tiny picture: a hammer, a star, a dark cloud. A teacher in a saree stands between them, pointing first to the slate and then to the cards. An arrow runs from the slate to the cards, showing alphabet first and words second. Soft tube-light glow mixed with evening light from the window. Labels: "ALPHABET" above the slate, "WORDS" above the flash cards.

key: A single candle is one sentence of a
name: ch12_pit_three_line_conversation
alt: Three traders in a trading pit exchange a short conversation, each speech bubble paired with a candle: a confident long white, a doubtful small star, and a firm long black.
scene: A lively mid-shot of an old-style trading pit with tiered wooden steps, paper slips scattered on the floor, a big price board on the wall behind and traders in coloured jackets. In the foreground three traders stand on the steps in a row from left to right, having a conversation. LEFT: a confident young trader in a bright green jacket throws his arm up and shouts, speech bubble "Higher!", and beside him floats a tall white candle. MIDDLE: an older trader in a grey jacket with spectacles raises one eyebrow and shrugs, speech bubble "Are we?", and beside him floats a tiny candle with a small body sitting above the first one, like a star. RIGHT: a stern woman trader in a dark red jacket folds her arms and shakes her head, speech bubble "No.", and beside her floats a tall black candle pushing down deep. A curved arrow links the three bubbles into a single exchange. In the background, other groups of traders are seen repeating the same three-step conversation with the same gestures, showing it happens again and again. Bright overhead lights and a busy atmosphere. Labels: "SENTENCE" under the first candle, "WHOLE EXCHANGE" along the curved arrow.

key: A phrasebook at the back of a language
name: ch12_phrasebook_learn_few
alt: A traveller with a thick phrasebook uses only a few marked phrases and looks up the rest when needed.
scene: A street scene in a bustling night market abroad, a narrow lane strung with paper lanterns and signboards in an unfamiliar script, at early evening. A young Indian traveller in a cotton shirt and a cross-body bag stands at a small food stall, holding a thick phrasebook open with many coloured sticky tabs sticking out of its side. The book has three bookmarked sections highlighted in bright yellow: the alphabet pages at the front, a single grammar page with a big rule box marked with an arrow, and a small handful of common phrases with stars beside them. The rest of the book, a huge block of pages, is shown thick and untouched, with a faint magnifying glass icon over it to show it is only for looking things up. He points confidently at the menu while saying a short phrase from one of his starred pages, and the friendly stall cook in an apron and headband smiles and nods, ladling noodles. Behind him on a bench, another tourist is buried in a giant stack of flash cards, looking overwhelmed and sweating. Warm lantern light and steam from the cooking pots. Labels: "ALPHABET" on the first tab, "CHECK THE TREND" on the grammar tab, and "LOOK UP THE REST" on the thick untouched block.

key: Wave 4 was the last place, during the
name: ch13_wave4_buyers_waiting_ledge
alt: On a mountain trail, people wait at a lower resting ledge where climbers once paused, ready to step in when the descending hikers return to it.
scene: A side view of a mountain trail zig-zagging up a rocky hill to a temple at the summit, the path marked with five numbered stone markers along the climb. Near the upper part of the trail, between markers 3 and 5, there is a broad flat ledge with a small tea stall, a bench and a big banyan tree, clearly remembered as a resting place where climbers paused on the way up; old footprints are pressed thickly into its dust. Now, at the top right, a group of hikers is coming back down the trail from the summit, carrying bags and walking sticks, with a downward arrow along their path. Waiting on the ledge below, a crowd of people stands ready with arms open and baskets, some who rested there before and some newcomers who missed it, a few waving and calling up to the descending hikers, and a thin horizontal line drawn across the ledge marks it as a floor. A tea seller pours chai from a height into small glasses, ready for the returning crowd. Evening golden light washes over the hill. Labels: "WAVE 4" on the ledge, "FLOOR FROM MEMORY" along the line, and "COMING BACK" beside the descending hikers.

key: A restaurant menu with 80 dishes
name: ch15_huge_menu_regulars_order_two
alt: In a busy restaurant a nervous newcomer is lost in an enormous menu while regulars at the next table order their two favourite dishes without looking.
scene: A warm interior of a popular old Udupi-style restaurant with marble-topped tables, steel tumblers, a ceiling fan and a waiter in a white uniform rushing with plates of dosa. On the LEFT, a young newcomer in a crisp office shirt sits alone with an enormous fold-out menu that unfolds like a map, so long it trails over the table edge and onto the floor, packed with tiny rows of dish names and little dish icons; he holds his head with one hand, eyes wide and anxious, sweat drops on his forehead, with a swirling question-mark bubble above him. On the RIGHT, at the next table, two cheerful regulars, an elderly man in a white veshti and his friend in a sleeveless sweater, have pushed their closed menus aside and simply hold up two fingers to the waiter, already smiling; above them a small thought bubble shows only two familiar dishes, a crisp dosa and a filter coffee, with stars. The waiter writes on his small pad without even looking up. Golden late-morning light through the windows and steam rising from the kitchen hatch. Labels: "80 CHOICES" on the giant menu, "THE TWO THAT WORK" over the regulars' thought bubble.

key: A friend who holds your car keys at a
name: ch15_friend_holds_keys_one_way
alt: A friend holding car keys at a party lets the driver choose the destination but stops him from going the wrong way down a one-way street.
scene: A night scene outside a house party in a residential lane, fairy lights on the balcony, music notes floating out of an open door, a few cars parked along the kerb. In the foreground, a cheerful young man in a party shirt points eagerly at a city map on his phone, choosing where to go next, while his sensible friend, a young woman in a denim jacket with a calm smile, holds up a bunch of car keys just out of his reach. Just beyond them the lane splits: on the right is a street with a large blue one-way sign whose arrow points away from them, and a dotted path from their car heads into it the wrong way, crossed out with a big red cross; on the left is a street where the one-way sign points the same way they want to drive, and a dotted path into it has a green tick. In a small thought bubble over the young woman, she pictures handing him the keys only for the left street. A neighbour's watchman sits on a stool by the gate with a torch, amused. Cool blue night light mixed with warm party glow. Labels: "YOU CHOOSE" over the young man's phone, "ONE WAY" on the blue sign, and "KEYS" beside the friend's raised hand.

key: Money management is deciding how much
name: ch16_road_trip_fuel_reserve
alt: Two cars head toward the same scenic destination; one is stranded empty after one breakdown, the other has spare fuel and money and carries on.
scene: A wide view of a long highway through a dry Deccan landscape, a beautiful hill fort with a flag drawn small on the horizon at the top right, a signpost pointing to it. Two cars are on the road. On the LEFT, a flashy red car is stopped on the hard shoulder with its bonnet up and steam rising from the engine, a flat tyre, and its fuel gauge inset showing empty; the driver, a young man in sunglasses, stands with empty pockets turned inside out and a jerrycan that is clearly empty, looking at the distant fort in despair. On the RIGHT, a modest grey hatchback is also pulled over with a small breakdown, but its driver, a middle-aged woman in a cotton saree, calmly pours fuel from one of two spare jerrycans in the boot, a small wallet with spare cash visible on the seat, a fuel gauge inset showing it refilled, and a mechanic on a motorbike already helping change a tyre. A dotted route line runs from both cars to the fort, but the left one stops short. Bright hot afternoon sun. Labels: "DESTINATION" on the signpost, "MONEY MANAGEMENT" over the spare jerrycans, and "STRANDED" over the red car.

key: Crossing a river on stepping stones
name: ch16_stepping_stones_step_size
alt: Two people cross a river on stepping stones: one taking small sure steps reaches the far bank, the other leaps too far and slips into the water.
scene: A wide view of a clear, fast-flowing mountain river with a line of round stepping stones crossing it from the left bank to the right bank, forested hills behind and a small shrine on the far bank. The route of stones is good and complete all the way across, drawn with a dotted line connecting them. On the upper line of stones, a careful woman in her forties in a salwar kameez with her dupatta tied around her waist steps from one stone to the next with small, sure steps, arms slightly out for balance, almost at the far bank with a calm face, and a small short arc between each of her steps. On the lower line, a confident young man in a tracksuit tries to jump over two stones at a time with a big leaping arc; his foot has slipped off a wet stone and he is splashing into the cold water, arms flailing, his phone flying from his pocket, a big splash and a shocked face. Fish dart away from the splash. A few villagers on the near bank point and laugh. Cool morning light with mist rising off the water. Labels: "GOOD ROUTE" above the line of stones, "SMALL STEPS" over the woman, and "LEAP TOO FAR" over the splash.

key: Diversification is umbrellas spread
name: ch16_umbrellas_one_head_vs_spread
alt: Four umbrellas held over one person leave others soaked, compared with four umbrellas spread over four people where only one gets wet when one blows away.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same rainy street corner during a heavy monsoon shower, puddles everywhere, an autorickshaw splashing past. LEFT panel: one man in a business suit stands in the middle holding four black umbrellas over his own head at once, stacked and overlapping, while three friends beside him in a row, a student, a vendor and an elderly woman with a cloth bag, stand completely unprotected and soaked, water streaming from their hair. A strong gust of wind blows from the side and turns all four umbrellas inside out together, so he gets soaked too. RIGHT panel: four people stand in a row, each holding their own umbrella of a different colour. The same strong gust turns just one umbrella inside out, and only that person gets wet, laughing it off, while the other three stay dry. Heavy rain streaks, grey sky, reflections in the puddles. Labels: "ALL ON ONE HEAD" at the top of the left panel, "SPREAD OUT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Timing is choosing which train
name: ch16_which_train_timing
alt: A traveller with a ticket already decided stands on a platform choosing between a crowded train leaving now at full price and the next one with a free seat.
scene: A wide view of a busy Indian railway platform with a steel roof, a big clock hanging from it, a tea stall with clay cups, and porters in red shirts carrying luggage on their heads. In the middle stands a young woman traveller in a kurta and jeans with a suitcase, holding a ticket envelope and a booked destination already circled on a route map in her other hand; small notes above her show her decision of where to go and how many tickets are already made. On the LEFT track, a train is pulling out right now, packed so full that passengers hang from the doors, with a large price tag dangling from the engine showing a high fare, the clock above showing the current time. On the RIGHT track, the next train waits quietly with an empty window seat clearly visible and a smaller price tag, and the station clock shows it will leave a little later. She looks from one to the other, thinking, with a thought bubble containing a small stopwatch. A chaiwala calls out nearby. Warm morning light filtering through the roof. Labels: "LEAVE NOW" over the left train, "NEXT TRAIN" over the right train, and "TIMING" above the traveller.

key: Buying concert tickets. Buy before the
name: ch16_concert_tickets_three_times
alt: Three fans buy concert tickets at three moments: cheaply before the line-up is announced, at full price on announcement day, and cheaper on resale after the price dips.
scene: A horizontal strip of three panels showing the same ticket booth outside an open-air concert ground, with a big blank poster frame on the wall behind. FIRST panel: the poster frame is empty with only question marks; a cautious college student in a hoodie buys a ticket cheaply, a small price tag, but a thought bubble shows him wondering if his favourite singer will even come. SECOND panel: the poster now shows a silhouetted band with a guitar and a microphone, the line-up announced, and a long eager queue forms; a young woman in a kurta pays a much higher price tag, but holds her ticket with confidence and a tick above her. THIRD panel: a few days later, a resale stall beside the booth shows a dip arrow on its price board, and an older man in a sweater buys a resold ticket for a little less than full price; a small inset at the corner shows the alternative ending, a board with a big red cross over an empty resale stall and the man walking away empty-handed. Bright evening light with stage lights warming up in the background. Labels: "EARLY" over the first panel, "CONFIRMED" over the second panel, and "PULLBACK" over the third panel.

key: Three friends independently tell you
name: ch16_three_friends_restaurant_fire
alt: Three friends each separately recommend the same restaurant, convincing a man to go, but when he walks in and sees the kitchen on fire he leaves at once.
scene: A two-part scene. LEFT part: a young man in a T-shirt sits on a park bench holding his phone, and three separate friends appear around him in three separate speech bubbles from different directions, each in a different setting: a woman at an office desk, a man on a scooter, and an older uncle at a tea stall, each giving a thumbs-up and pointing to the same restaurant icon, a little plate with a star. Dotted lines from the three bubbles converge on him, and his face lights up, convinced. RIGHT part: the same young man has just walked through the glass door of the restaurant, and through the serving hatch the kitchen is plainly on fire with big flames and smoke, the cook waving a towel. He has already spun around mid-step, heading straight back out the door with a fast exit arrow, eyebrows up, not waiting to order. A small sign on the door shows the restaurant's name as just a star. Bright daylight on the left, smoky orange light on the right. Labels: "THREE SIGNALS" over the converging bubbles, "SUPPORT BREAKS" over the burning kitchen, and "EXIT" beside the arrow.

key: Buying a used car. Market order
name: ch16_used_car_four_orders
alt: Four buyers at a used-car lot show four order types: paying the sticker price, leaving an offer, buying only if the price rises past a level, and buying the moment a price is touched.
scene: A wide view of a roadside used-car lot with bunting, a small office cabin and a row of the same model of second-hand white hatchback, each with a price card on the windscreen. A cheerful dealer with a moustache, gold chain and a notebook stands near the cabin. Four buyers are shown left to right. FIRST: a hurried businessman in a suit hands over a bundle of cash at the sticker price and drives away immediately, a speed line behind the car. SECOND: a thrifty retired teacher writes her offer on a slip of paper and hands it to the dealer with a phone icon showing call me, and a small clock with cobwebs shows she may wait forever. THIRD: a young man in a cricket jersey watches the price card on a car through binoculars, with a thought bubble of an upward arrow crossing a line, ready to buy only once the price climbs above it, showing it is in demand. FOURTH: a woman in a saree stands with one foot through the cabin doorway, cash ready, as the price card on the car flips to her figure, and a small arrow shows the card nudging slightly higher by the time she arrives. Bright midday sun. Labels: "MARKET" over the first buyer, "LIMIT" over the second, and "STOP" over the third.

key: The same item sold in two shops across
name: ch17_cash_shop_vs_collection_shop
alt: Two shops across a street sell the same sack of rice, one for cash today and one for collection in two months at a slightly higher price, with a trader closing the gap and both prices meeting on collection day.
scene: A wide street view of a wholesale grain market lane with two shops facing each other across a narrow street, sacks of rice stacked outside both. LEFT shop: a sign shows a sack icon with a sun for today, and a shopkeeper in a white vest hands a sack to a customer who pays cash on the spot. RIGHT shop: an identical sack with a sign showing a calendar two months ahead, and the shopkeeper in a cap writes a slip for later collection; its price board is a little higher, and a small inset shows money sitting locked in a safe to explain the extra. In the middle of the street, a quick young trader in a kurta with a cloth bag runs between the two shops, buying from the left and selling to the right, with a looping arrow between the price boards and the gap between them shrinking. At the bottom, a small inset of the same street on collection day shows both price boards showing the same figure, the two shopkeepers shaking hands across the road. Bright morning light, porters with handcarts passing. Labels: "CASH TODAY" over the left shop, "FUTURES" over the right shop, and "GAP CLOSES" over the running trader.

key: A bond is a fixed stream of payments
name: ch17_fixed_coupon_buys_less
alt: An elderly man's fixed monthly payment fills a full shopping bag when prices are low and only half a bag when bread, fuel and metal get dearer, so fewer people want to pay for the bond.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same retired gentleman, a man in his seventies with a white moustache, cardigan and walking stick, at the counter of the same kirana shop. In both panels he holds the same envelope with an identical stack of notes, and a small certificate pinned to his cardigan shows a fixed payment amount. LEFT panel: price tags on bread, a can of cooking oil, a bag of rice and a steel pot are low, and his envelope buys a full, overflowing shopping bag that he carries happily. RIGHT panel: the same items now have big new price tags with upward arrows, and the same envelope buys only half a bag; he holds it looking disappointed. In a small inset at the bottom right, a young investor at a desk pushes a bond certificate away and lowers the price tag on it, showing nobody wants to pay as much for those fixed payments. The shopkeeper behind the counter shrugs apologetically. Warm shop light. Labels: "FIXED PAYMENT" over the envelope, "PRICES UP" over the right shelf, and "BOND PRICE DROPS" beside the inset.

key: When the dollar gets stronger, the same
name: ch17_strong_dollar_cheaper_gold
alt: A balance scale weighs dollar notes against a gold bar and an oil barrel; as each note grows heavier, fewer are needed, and the gold bar moves first while the barrel follows.
scene: A clean view of a big old brass balance scale standing on a wooden counter in a bullion dealer's shop, glass cabinets with jewellery behind, a ceiling fan. On the left pan sits a pile of green banknotes marked only with a dollar sign. On the right pan sits a gold bar and, just behind it, a small oil barrel. The scene is shown in two stages left to right as a before-and-after. In the first stage, a tall pile of thin notes balances the gold and the barrel. In the second stage, each note has become visibly thicker and heavier, drawn with a small flexing arm icon, so only a short pile of notes is needed and the price tags on the gold bar and barrel drop with downward arrows. The gold bar's price tag is already falling while the barrel's tag is only just beginning to tip, with a little numbered order showing the gold moving first. The dealer, an older man in a crisp white kurta with spectacles on a chain, weighs it all with a thoughtful expression, while a customer in a saree watches. Warm golden shop light. Labels: "STRONGER DOLLAR" over the heavier notes, "GOLD FIRST" over the gold bar.

key: A utility is like a bond with a building
name: ch17_utility_and_gold_miner
alt: A power plant shown as a bond certificate with a building attached, rising as interest rates fall, and a gold mine shown as a gold bar with a mine attached, whose profits swing more than the gold price.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a large bond certificate with a ribbon stands upright like a wall, and attached to its back is a power station with cooling towers and electric pylons, as if the certificate grew a building. Steady coins drip from a pipe at the bottom into a bucket, showing steady payouts. A big loan chain trails from the building to a bank. A thermometer-style dial labelled with a percentage sign beside it drops, and both the certificate and the power station rise up on a lift platform together with an upward arrow, while the loan chain lightens. RIGHT panel: a large shiny gold bar lies on the ground with a working mine shaft, conveyor belt and a few miners in helmets attached to it. A small arrow beside the gold bar shows it rising a little, while a much bigger arrow beside the mine's profit chest shows it jumping a lot more, and a miner in a hard hat cheers. Small inset: the gold bar's small dip makes the profit chest drop sharply. Clear midday light. Labels: "UTILITY" over the left panel, "GOLD MINER" over the right panel, and "RATES FALL" beside the dial.

key: Normally falling rates are a tailwind
name: ch17_tailwind_failing_engine
alt: A small motorboat with a strong wind at its back still slows and sinks lower because its engine is sputtering, while a sailboat beside it flies ahead.
scene: A wide seascape on a choppy grey-blue sea near a harbour, gulls overhead and a lighthouse on the right horizon. A strong tailwind blows from left to right, drawn as long flowing wind lines across the whole picture. In the foreground, a small motorboat painted with a stock-chart zig-zag on its side struggles: its outboard engine at the back coughs black smoke and sputters, a few broken gears flying out, and the boat sits low in the water, slowing, a downward arrow beside its hull. Its captain, a worried man in a yellow raincoat, bangs on the engine with a spanner while the wind pushes uselessly at his back. Just beside it, a sleek white sailboat with a big full sail flies ahead on the same wind, a long upward-forward arrow, its sailor relaxed and grinning; a small certificate flag on the mast shows it is a bond. A small inset at the top left shows a falling price-tag arrow for goods, labelled with a shrinking factory, explaining why the engine is failing. Overcast stormy light with a beam of sun on the sailboat. Labels: "TAILWIND" along the wind lines, "PROFITS FAILING" beside the engine, and "DEFLATION" in the top-left inset.

key: Daily weigh-ins jump around with what
name: ch18_daily_vs_weekly_weighin
alt: A man's daily scale readings jump up and down with what he ate, while a weekly chart on the fridge shows the steady real direction, so he waits before buying new clothes.
scene: A cosy bathroom-and-hallway scene in a small apartment in the morning. On the LEFT, a man in his forties in a towel and vest stands on a bathroom scale, peering down at it; around the scale, seven small floating thought bubbles show what he ate on each previous day, a plate of biryani, a bowl of salad, a box of laddoos, a glass of water, and each bubble has the scale reading jumping up or down with little zig-zag arrows. On the RIGHT, on the fridge door in the hallway, a calendar chart with one big dot per week forms a smooth gently sloping line, held up with fruit-shaped magnets. His wife in a nightie points at the weekly chart while he holds a shopping bag from a clothes shop, about to rush out, and she gently holds his arm back with a patient smile. A small wall clock and a tulsi pot sit on the windowsill, and a dotted arrow runs from the jumpy scale to the calm fridge chart to show which one to trust. Soft early morning light. Labels: "DAILY NOISE" over the jumping bubbles, "WEEKLY TREND" on the fridge chart, and "WAIT" beside the shopping bag.

key: Two thermometers in the same room
name: ch18_fast_slow_thermometers
alt: Two thermometers on the same wall, one quick and one slow; when the quick one reads warmer the room is heating, and a very large gap means the heating can't last at that pace.
scene: A warm interior of a living room in winter, with a glowing room heater in the corner, a sofa with a shawl draped over it, and a window showing a foggy morning outside. On the wall side by side hang two large thermometers. The left one is thin and twitchy with a tiny bulb, drawn with a small running-rabbit icon at its top; its red column has shot up high. The right one is thick and heavy with a large bulb, drawn with a small tortoise icon at its top; its column has risen only a little. A bright bracket between the two red tops measures the gap. An inset bubble above shows the same pair a few minutes later with an even bigger gap and a small warning triangle, and the heater's coil glowing almost white hot, steam coming from the window, suggesting it cannot keep warming at this speed. A father in a sweater with a cup of tea looks at the gap, while his little son in a monkey cap holds his hands toward the heater. Cosy orange light from the heater, cool grey light from the window. Labels: "FAST" over the left thermometer, "SLOW" over the right thermometer, and "GAP" on the bracket.

key: the Summation Index is the season
name: ch18_weather_days_vs_season
alt: A long strip of daily weather tiles through summer with a few cold days that don't end it, and a running tally jar that finally tips negative as the season turns.
scene: A long horizontal strip of daily square tiles runs across the picture like a calendar wall in a village school, each tile showing the day's weather as a little drawing: many sunny tiles with bright suns, a cluster of three cold, cloudy tiles in the middle, then more sunny tiles, and toward the right end a steadily growing run of cold, foggy and rainy tiles as autumn arrives with falling leaves. Under the strip sits a big glass jar on a shelf: for every day colder than usual a blue marble is dropped in, for every warmer day an orange marble, and a level line on the jar shows the running balance. Under the cold cluster in the middle, the jar level dips a little but stays on the warm side. Under the right end, the jar level crosses below a painted zero line, and a small autumn tree beside it turns orange and drops its leaves. A schoolteacher in a woollen shawl drops a blue marble in while children in sweaters watch. Light shifts from warm summer gold on the left to cool grey on the right. Labels: "TODAY" above one tile, "SEASON" on the jar, and "SEASON CHANGES" where the level crosses zero.

key: Counting stocks is counting hands raised
name: ch18_hands_raised_money_held
alt: In a meeting hall many people with small coin purses raise their hands to buy, while a few people on the other side hold huge bags of money to sell.
scene: A wide view of a crowded cooperative society meeting hall with rows of plastic chairs, a ceiling fan and a banner above the stage. A vote is happening. On the LEFT side of the hall, a large group of about twenty ordinary members, farmers, shopkeepers and students, cheerfully raise their hands high to buy, but each one holds only a tiny cloth coin purse with a couple of coins. On the RIGHT side, only four people raise their hands to sell: two wealthy-looking men in suits, a woman in a silk saree and an elderly trader with a turban, and each of them clutches a huge, bulging sack of money at their feet, the sacks so big they tower over the chairs. A secretary on the stage, a middle-aged man with spectacles, tallies on a blackboard: the count of hands is clearly higher on the buying side, but beside it a big old balance scale on the stage tips heavily toward the selling side under the weight of the sacks. A peon carries a tray of tea through the aisle. Bright tube-light lighting. Labels: "MORE HANDS" over the buyers, "MORE MONEY" over the sellers' sacks, and "VOLUME" on the scale.
